<h>Lectio 1</h>
De libro primo Regum
<r>1 Reg 19:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> Locútus est autem Saul ad Iónatham fílium suum et ad omnes servos suos ut occíderent David. Porro Iónathas fílius Saul diligébat David valde.
<n>2</n> Et indicávit Iónathas David dicens: Quærit Saul pater meus occídere te; quaprópter obsérva te, quæso, mane, et manébis clam, et abscondéris.
<n>3</n> Ego autem egrédiens stabo iuxta patrem meum in agro ubicúmque fúeris; et ego loquar de te ad patrem meum, et quodcúmque vídero, nuntiábo tibi.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Præparáte corda vestra Dómino, et servíte illi soli:
* Et liberábit vos de mánibus inimicórum vestrórum.
<r>℣.</r> Convertímini ad eum in toto corde vestro, et auférte deos aliénos de médio vestri.
<r>℟.</r> Et liberábit vos de mánibus inimicórum vestrórum.

<h>Reading 1</h>
Lesson from the first book of Samuel
<r>1 Sam 19:1-3</r>
<n>1</n> And Saul spoke to Jonathan his son and to all his servants, that they should kill David. But Jonathan the son of Saul loved David exceedingly.
<n>2</n> And Jonathan told David, saying: Saul my father seeketh to kill thee: wherefore look to thyself, I beseech thee, in the morning, and thou shalt abide in a secret place and shalt be hid.
<n>3</n> And I will go out and stand beside my father in the field where thou art: and I will speak of thee to my father, and whatsoever I shall see, I will tell thee.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve Him Only
* And He will deliver you out of the hand of your enemies.
<r>℣.</r> Return unto Him with all your hearts, and put away the strange gods from among you.
<r>℟.</r> And He will deliver you out of the hand of your enemies.

<h>Lectio 2</h>
<r>1 Reg 19:4-6</r>
<n>4</n> Locútus est ergo Iónathas de David bona ad Saul patrem suum dixítque ad eum: Ne pecces, rex, in servum tuum David, quia non peccávit tibi, et ópera eius bona sunt tibi valde.
<n>5</n> Et pósuit ánimam suam in manu sua et percússit Philisthǽum, et fecit Dóminus salútem magnam univérso Israéli. Vidísti et lætátus es; quare ergo peccas in sánguine innóxio interfíciens David, qui est absque culpa?
<n>6</n> Quod cum audísset Saul, placátus voce Iónathæ iurávit: Vivit Dóminus, quia non occidétur.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Percússit Saul mille, et David decem míllia:
quia manus Dómini erat cum illo: percússit Philisthǽum,
* Et ábstulit oppróbrium ex Israël.
<r>℣.</r> Nonne iste est David, de quo canébant in choro, dicéntes: Saul percússit mille, et David decem míllia in míllibus suis?
<r>℟.</r> Et ábstulit oppróbrium ex Israël.

<h>Reading 2</h>
<r>1 Sam 19:4-6</r>
<n>4</n> And Jonathan spoke good things of David to Saul his father: and said to him: Sin not, O king, against thy servant, David, because he hath not sinned against thee, and his works are very good towards thee.
<n>5</n> And he put his life in his hand, and slew the Philistine, and the Lord wrought great salvation for all Israel. Thou sawest it and didst rejoice. Why therefore wilt thou sin against innocent blood by killing David, who is without fault?
<n>6</n> And when Saul heard this he was appeased with the words of Jonathan, and swore: As the Lord liveth he shall not be slain.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>℟.</r> Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.
because the hand of the Lord was with him, he smote the Philistine,
* And took away the reproach from Israel.
<r>℣.</r> Is not this David in míllibus suis? Did they not sing one to another of him in dances, saying: Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands?
<r>℟.</r> And took away the reproach from Israel.

<r>1 Reg 19:8-10</r>

<n>9</n> Et factus est spíritus Dómini malus in Saul. Sedébat autem in domo sua et tenébat lánceam; porro David psallébat manu sua.
<n>10</n> Nisúsque est Saul confígere David láncea in paríete, et declinávit David a fácie Saul; láncea autem, casso vúlnere, perláta est in paríetem. Et David fugit et salvátus est nocte illa.

<r>℟.</r> Ubi cecidérunt fortes Israël.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

b.3f1a827d03:
<h>Oratio</h>
<c>K</c>ýrie, eléison. Christe, eléison. Kýrie, eléison.
<n><k>Pater Noster</k> dicitur secreto usque ad <k>Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:</k></n>
<c>P</c>ater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
<r>℣.</r> Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
<r>℟.</r> Sed líbera nos a malo.

<r>℣.</r> Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
<r>℟.</r> Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>D</c>eus, qui diligéntibus te bona invisibília præparásti: infúnde córdibus nostris tui amóris afféctum; ut te in ómnibus et super ómnia diligéntes, promissiónes tuas, quæ omne desidérium súperant, consequámur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.8b52f817cb:
<h>Prayer</h>
<c>L</c>ord have mercy upon us, Christ have mercy upon us, Lord have mercy upon us.
<n><k>Our Father</k> is said silently until <k>And lead us not into temptation:</k>.</n>
<c>O</c>ur Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.
<r>℣.</r> And lead us not into temptation:
<r>℟.</r> But deliver us from evil.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> God, Who hast prepared for them that love thee such good things as pass man's understanding; pour into our hearts such love toward thee, that we, loving thee in all things and above all things, may obtain thy promises, which exceed all that we can desire.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.b6a7f05503:
<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>exto Kaléndas Iúlii Luna vicésima secúnda. Anno Dómini 2027
<h>R</h>omæ, in monte Cǽlio, sanctórum Mártyrum Ioánnis et Pauli fratrum, quorum primus erat præpósitus domus, secúndus primicérius Constántiæ Vírginis, fíliæ Constantíni Imperatóris, et ambo póstea, sub Iuliáno Apóstata, martýrii palmam, cædénte gládio, percepérunt.
<h>A</h>pud Tridéntum sancti Vigílii Epíscopi, qui, cum relíquias idololatríæ pénitus exstirpáre conarétur, ídeo, pro Christi nómine, a feris et bárbaris homínibus percússus lápidum imbre, martýrium implévit.
<h>A</h>pud Valencénas, in Gállia, pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Sálvii, qui éxstitit Engolisménsis Epíscopus, et Supérii.
<h>C</h>órdubæ, in Hispánia, natális sancti Pelágii adolescéntuli, qui, ob confessiónem fídei, Regis Saracenórum Abdaraméni iussu forcípibus férreis membrátim præcísus, martýrium suum glorióse consummávit.
<h>B</h>ellícii, in Gállia, sancti Anthélmi, qui ex maióris Carthúsiæ Prióre, factus est eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopus.
<h>I</h>n pago Pictaviénsi sancti Maxéntii, Presbýteri et Confessóris; qui miráculis cláruit.
<h>T</h>hessalonícæ sancti David Eremítæ.
<h>E</h>ódem die sanctæ Perseverándæ Vírginis.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.aa9ee04359:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>J</c>une 26th 2027, the 22nd day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, upon the Celian Mount, the holy brethren John and Paul, both martyrs. John was provost of the household, and Paul chief steward of the Virgin Constantia, daughter of the Emperor Constantine. Under the Emperor Julian the Apostate they both received the palm of martyrdom by the sword.
<h>A</h>t Trent, [about the year 400,] the holy Vigilius, Bishop [of that see,] who, because he was striving to stamp out utterly the last remains of idolatry, was stoned by savage men, and so compassed martyrdom for Christ's Name's sake.
<h>A</h>t Valenciennes, [at the beginning of the ninth century,] the holy martyrs Salvius, Bishop of Angoulême, and Superius.
<h>A</h>t Cordova, in Spain, [in the tenth century,] the holy child Pelagius, who crowned his confession of the faith with a glorious martyrdom, by being torn to pieces with iron pincers, by order of Abdu'l-Rahman, King of the Saracens.
<h>A</h>t Bellay, in Gaul, [in the year 1178,] holy Anthelm, who, from being Prior of the Grande Chartreuse, was made Bishop of that city.
<h>A</h>t Poitou, [in the sixth century,] the holy Priest and Confessor Maxentius, who was famous for miracles.
<h>A</h>t Thessalonica, [likewise in the sixth century,] the holy Hermit David.
<h>O</h>n the same day, [in the sixth century also,] the holy Virgin Perseveranda.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
